summary: The strongest face-on subject read in the wax row: a crowned heraldic serpent coils round a flush tsavorite on the native 020 escutcheon, inside a 42-bead bordure on a pounced field, with feathered mantling pouring off both sides. The build is clean at three resolutions and the template lifts with 0 patches. It does not ship. The lost-wax land-width gate is missing. Nothing asserts or names the boss's 0.6 mm lip, the proud stamps under 0.8 mm (nine of the ten proud stamp families: pearls 0.68, fangs 0.36-0.40 to a point, tongue 0.26-0.36, brow 0.40, lip scales 0.38-0.42, crown jewels 0.30, crown band 0.65, the pointed crown points), the 0.44 mm beads or the painted tail's 0.6 mm tip. That alone is an automatic revise. The craft also falls short where Logan looks hardest. The head is a smooth, scale-less duck bill with stamps pasted on: a bead eye whose pupil does not read face-on, sticker lip scales and droplet fangs. The flat-topped forked tongue vanishes face-on and is a Y bracket at 3/4. The 3.8 mm crown reads as three dots at 300 px, and face-on the shield reads closer to the Slytherin crest than to a crowned basilisk. At 3/4 the painted body's flanks comb vertically and its edges fringe. The hackle roots on the head walls are truncated slabs, the hackle-to-scale morph is a corrugated band, and the palm scutes are tread blocks. The author's 'about 2 mm' relief measures 1.385 mm. Score 6.5 against a self-score of 7.5. One focused round on the head, crown, tongue and walls, plus the land-width gate, can reach 7.5.
strengths: Face-on the composition is clear and heraldic: an S-coiled serpent, its head under the chief, its body round the stone's right end and underside, its tail curling into the shield's point. face.png and face-300.png read 'serpent on a shield' without a caption.
One theme face to palm: the crest on the table, feathered mantling that morphs to keeled scale on the shoulders, round scales on the head walls and shank, and ventral scutes on the palm.

The native, unmirrored 020 keeps its hard table edge and its cusped chief and point (bare-vs-finished.png). It is the only escutcheon in the collection, a silhouette distinct from Arachne's band, Draco's kite and Fenrir's trillion.
The tsavorite sits in a made flush bur with a through pilot and is visible from every face-side view. The stone report is clean: 1 of 1 previewed, 0 warnings, 0 tight pairs.
The small-scale texture is well judged face-on: the 42-bead bordure at 0.66 mm pitch and the pounced field give the table heraldic density above Caiman's.

The engineering is clean. It is watertight at 384 x 192, 768 x 320 and 1536 x 448 (1,781,600 triangles), with 0 degenerates, 0 self-crossings, 21/21 stamps struck and 0 DFM findings. It fields Castable in wax at a 1.677 mm wall, lifts with 0 patches at 2.90 MB, and cold reloads identically.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: One heraldic basilisk throughout: the crowned serpent on the table, feathered mantling that turns to keeled scale 70-110 deg off the head, round scales and shields on the head walls and shank, and ventral scutes on the palm. Nothing is scattered. Face-on, the mantling fans read as palm fronds or laurel rather than hackles (item 7).

checklist.item: Figurative motifs are stamps or parts with true outlines, not painted smudges
checklist.reason: The serpent's body and head are painted, but from exact spline SDFs, so face-on the silhouette is crisp and nowhere blurs into 'arrows'. The crown, eye, fangs, tongue and lip scales are stamps. Two render faults undercut it. At 3/4 the body's steep flanks comb into vertical streaks, with a sawtooth fringe along the plinth edge (shoulder.png 1100-1320 x 460-740, stones.png 420-900 x 900-1160). The flat-topped tongue stamp is invisible face-on (items 3 and 5).

checklist.item: Faces and eyes are allowed when they read well; a poor face is a defect
checklist.reason: A poor face. The head is a smooth, scale-less dome with two flat jaw plates, and at 3/4 it reads as a duck bill (stones.png 300-760 x 230-640). The eye is a proud glossy bead on top of the skull with no socket. Its 0.26 mm slit pupil does not read face-on, and the brow is a flat lens floating above it. The five lip scales are pasted-on ellipses and the 0.6-0.7 mm fangs read as water droplets. There is no menace: no brow overhang, no head plates, no recessed gape.

checklist.item: Stones sit in made settings and are visible
checklist.reason: The tsavorite marquise 8 x 4 is flush in a 0.9 mm boss with a made bur (SolidKind::Flush) and a through pilot. It is visible in the hero, face and stones views, and the pilot shows in the bore (palm.png) as expected. The boss lip is only 0.6 mm (5.2 x 9.2 mm boss on a 4 x 8 stone), which item 1 must widen or name.

checklist.item: Shoulder ornament is not cut off toward the face
checklist.reason: The hackles emerge from under the table edge on both sides (face.png) and run unbroken to the morph; nothing ends in a hard line short of the table. Their roots on the diagonal head walls are a separate craft defect (item 6).

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason: Five mechanical reads. (a) The forked tongue is a flat-topped, vertical-walled Y slab (stones.png 340-490 x 520-600). (b) The hackle roots on the head walls are truncated slabs with vertically striated ends (hero.png 470-650 x 760-900). (c) The palm's belly scutes are flat rounded rectangles like a tank tread, ending square on the shank sides (palm.png 400-1250 x 380-560, reverse.png 1170-1440 x 400-820). (d) The 0.07 mm pounce plateau draws L-shaped ledges and leaves a sliver island (face.png 430-700 x 490-600, 713-847 x 1057-1090). (e) The painted body's flanks comb vertically at 3/4.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: bare-vs-finished.png shows the 020's table edge, cusped chief and point intact. The bordure sits 0.62 mm inside the edge and nothing rolls the rim. The prism corner under the point still runs as a crisp vertical arris down the end wall (side.png).

checklist.item: A silhouette distinct from the other Bestiarium rings
checklist.reason: It is the only escutcheon in the Bestiarium: an upright shield head on a plain shank, unlike Arachne's keyframed band, Draco's kite and Fenrir's trillion. It is a crest ring, not a snake-head plan, so it stays clear of Serpentarium's viper-head signet. The risk is recorded under the 300 px read: face-on, a serpent in an S round a green stone on a shield reads as the Slytherin crest.

checklist.item: Reads as its subject at a glance at 300 px, without the caption
checklist.reason: face-300.png reads 'serpent on a shield', but the 3.8 mm crown is three dots (about 36 px wide) and nothing says 'king' or 'basilisk', so the read is closer to the Hogwarts house crest. hero-300.png, the image the sheet uses, loses the head and the crown entirely; it reads as a coil round a green stone in a dotted shield.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: Large forms: the shield, the S-serpent and the stone. Medium: the head, the mantling fans and the flank scales. Small: beads, pits, scale keels and barbs. Face-on, the density and the subject read exceed Caiman's hero. At 3/4 the shoulders turn noisy rather than dense, with glinting fragments at the hackle roots; items 5-7 address that.

punch_list.zone: report.json and the gate list (bestiarium_basiliscus.rs:1179-1188); seat 'Tsavorite, flush' at theta 91.3 deg; every proud stamp; the painted tail and bordure
punch_list.change: Assert the lost-wax land widths. Add a land_widths block and a matching gate term. Give the boss lip and each proud stamp its measured minimum land, and give the painted body its minimum width along the spine. Either raise a feature to at least 0.8 mm or name it as an exception with its bench treatment. Concretely: widen the boss stock from 1.2 to 1.6 mm (diameter 5.6, long axis 9.6), or name the 0.6 mm lip as the burnished lip over the girdle. Raise GIRTH.1 from 0.3 to 0.4 so the tail ends at 0.8 mm, or name the tip. Name the pointed features (crown points, fangs, tongue tines) and the fine lands (pearls, brow, lip scales, crown jewels, beads) as investment-detail exceptions at or above the 0.15 mm floor.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json carries land_widths, with one row per proud feature (name, minimum land in mm, and either 'at or above 0.8' or the exception text). gates has an entry 'lost-wax land widths at or above 0.8 mm or named' that is true, and it goes false if any row under 0.8 lacks an exception. Both the --draft --verify run and the export run pass every gate.
